title: Sterling Silver 1926 Sesquicentennial Spoon Independence Hall Weisgerber 19.4g
description_html:
Sterling Silver Souvenir Spoon — 1926 Sesqui-Centennial International Exposition, Philadelphia — Signing of the Declaration of Independence

An official-style souvenir of the 1926 Sesqui-Centennial International Exposition, the world's fair held in Philadelphia for the 150th anniversary of American independence — the same celebration that produced the collectible 1926 Sesquicentennial half dollar. The bowl shows Independence Hall bracketed by "1776" and a Sesqui-Centennial of American Independence scroll; the handle carries a full-relief rendering of the Signing of the Declaration of Independence, with the Liberty Bell, crossed flags, and a run of stars down the reverse of the tip. "SIGNING THE DECLARATION OF AMERICAN INDEPENDENCE" is lettered in relief along the stem back.

Marked "© C.H. WEISGERBER" — Charles H. Weisgerber (1867-1932) was the Philadelphia artist who painted "Birth of Our Nation's Flag" and founded the Betsy Ross Memorial Association that saved the Betsy Ross House; he licensed Revolutionary-themed designs like this one in support of that mission.

Details:

  • Sterling silver (.925), stamped STERLING with the Weisgerber copyright.
  • Notably substantial for a souvenir spoon: weighed at 19.45 grams on a digital scale (many run 10-14g); measures 5.75 inches.
  • No monogram.

Condition: relief detail sharp throughout with attractive natural patina in the recesses; bright bowl with light tarnish consistent with age. No dents, no bends, no repairs. Please review all photos, including both hallmark close-ups.

Ships boxed with padding — never in a plain envelope — so it arrives exactly as pictured.

A heavy, high-relief piece for collectors of 1926 Sesquicentennial memorabilia, Philadelphia and Independence Hall history, or Revolutionary War and Declaration of Independence themes.
